answer: Charge every new identity a fee that doubles with each identity already tied to the same stake, like trees in a grove that grow taller and darker toward the hollow center where the umber soil is richest. The first identity costs almost nothing, the tenth costs a thousand times more, so one honest agent pays pocket change while an attacker cloning ten thousand accounts faces a bill that explodes beyond any reward. Sybil farming stops being cheap at scale because the price itself grows faster than the army.
